_schema: Implementation-review record (DSv4-Flash pilot, Phase A). Follows the kernel-provenance + kernel<->cost-model reconciliation gates. Records: (1) CORRECTNESS re-verification of every authored kernel against its EXTERNAL torch oracle, across all costed shapes and both normal + heavier-tailed ('realistic') distributions, at a tight tolerance; (2) the resolved kernel revisions; (3) re-authoring / routing decisions; (4) the PERF-vs-roofline measurement status. Correctness here is MICROBENCH scope (current-target/E2E verification PENDING).
reverified_at_note: de48f87 is the CORRECTNESS re-verification commit (a SEPARATE identity from the timing job in perf_vs_roofline.raw_record, R2-P1); it binds the oracle re-runs below, not the measured latency.

correctness_reverification.method: ran each kernel's microbench vs its torch oracle (bench_*.py) on the venv; additionally re-verified the compressor at ALL THREE costed shapes (R=128/D=512, R=8/D=512, R=8/D=128) under normal AND heavy-tailed inputs with tol relerr<=1e-4, cos>=0.999999.

kernels.result: cos>=0.99999994, relerr~1e-7 at ALL 3 costed shapes, normal + heavy-tail
kernels.verdict: PASS (shape-coverage gap CLOSED: was verified only at R=128/D=512)

kernels.result: scalar cos>=0.9999 PASS; AMX cos=0.999963 which is > 0.9999 so it ALSO PASSES the stated 0.9999 bar (the earlier '< 0.9999 FAIL' claim was a FALSE inequality, F4). Neither variant has a declared elementwise-error / discrete-decision acceptance yet.
kernels.verdict: SURFACED candidate, NOT certified: cited oracle (dsa_sparse_attention_cpu) is STALE (no sink); the real oracle is inline in bench_sparse_attend.py; AMX differs in BF16 rounding; donor dispatch is NOT proven. Preserve the scalar's ~3.55x M=1 advantage; do not delete with a blanket regression label.

decisions: sparse_attend: keep as a SURFACED candidate (not certified). The scalar RETAINS a ~3.55x M=1 advantage over torch (do not delete with a blanket regression label). Donor dispatch is NOT yet proven — needs a concrete donor entry point + sink/mask/two-source/KV-layout capability check + dispatch evidence. Cited oracle is stale (no sink); real oracle is inline in bench_sparse_attend.py.

compressor / indexer_logits: FAITHFUL stage FRAGMENTS; F1 (compressor masked-NaN) and F2 (indexer dispatch numerics) were REAL bugs now fixed + verified. Remaining projections/RoPE/Hadamard/quant/overlap/decode-state stay EXPLICITLY-UNMODELED per kernel_provenance.json.

ROI queue is NOT closed (F7): the no-more-ROI / DRAM-wall-proven claims are retracted; ranked open hypotheses recorded (indexer M=1 regression, compressor channel/task partitioning, small-S top-k simplification, indexer conversion/pack removal, donor-dispatch proof, R=8 pool shapes).
resolved kept-pass revisions from authoring commits (topk=17dbb0d, compressor=ccded85, sinkhorn=ccded85, combine=dbfbcfa, sparse_attend=eb4ecdf); historical result coordinates retained.

perf_vs_roofline.raw_record: SLURM job 384414, log /scratch/bkaul/dsa_perf_sweep_384414.log, node pcl-sprh09.sc.intel.com (DDR5-5600), 2026-10-09; run_dsa_perf_sweep.sbatch; 3 reps/bench (median of unique REP ids 1/2/3); OMP 64thr bound once, numactl NUMA0. This is the CURRENT timing identity (R2-P1), distinct from the correctness re-verification commit (reverified_at); the superseded first run (job 384372, node pcl-sprh11) is retained as history only, not joined.
perf_vs_roofline.measured_sweep: results/perf_sweep.json (median cpp_ms per op across M=1/8/16/32/64)
perf_vs_roofline.report: reports/dsv4_roofline_vs_measured_emr.txt (per op: roofline ideal vs measured vs off-ceiling across the full M sweep, with plateau explanation)
perf_vs_roofline.ceiling_basis: NOMINAL machine peak (BW 358.4 GB/s, FP32 7.78 TF / AMX 124.5 TF). off_ceiling = measured_median / nominal_ideal; the node reaches ~60-77% of nominal DRAM BW so a BW-bound op is ~1.3-1.7x off the wall alone; small ops are latency/dispatch-bound (far from roof by construction).
perf_vs_roofline.plateau_finding: OPEN — NOT a proven plateau (F7). RE-MEASURED on the fixed kernels (SLURM 384414, parse_perf_sweep.py validated). F2 side-effect: the single-contract tiled indexer COLLAPSED the M=1 regression 1.023ms -> 0.100ms (the old bmm path carried a full score round-trip). F3 fixed: sparse scalar column now correct [0.068,0.46,0.894,1.793,3.64] (was the Torch-ref column); the scalar's ~3.6x M=1 advantage over torch is no longer hidden. Useful throughput is still far below reference BW, so DRAM saturation is NOT established; competing causes (N-only parallelism, exp throughput, cache residency, conversion/pack/GEMM/epilogue split, small-S top-k chunk cap S/k=2) remain ranked ROI hypotheses.
perf_vs_roofline.verdict: Correctness bugs F1 (compressor masked-NaN) + F2 (indexer dispatch numerics) FIXED + verified; F9 guards added; F6 join contracts corrected; F3 ingestion validated; F7 no-ROI/BW-wall claims RETRACTED (ROI OPEN + ranked). Off-ceiling is a DIAGNOSTIC vs the nominal roof, NOT a plateau. sparse_attend stays a SURFACED candidate (donor dispatch unproven).

overall: Addressing the GPT Astra 6 implementation review (CHANGES REQUIRED, F1-F9). CORRECTNESS bugs FIXED + verified: F1 compressor masked-position NaN (now finite all-ones on the published overlap case), F2 indexer dispatch numerics (single matmul contract -> identical selection across M). F9 shape guards added to all 6 kernels. F6 join contracts corrected (top-k INT64 output 262,144 B; indexer BF16 compute with FP32 public storage). F7 no-more-ROI / DRAM-wall claims RETRACTED -> ranked open hypotheses. F4 false cosine inequality corrected. Perf being RE-MEASURED on the fixed kernels (SLURM 384414). OPEN/surfaced: declared per-op acceptance policy + fail-closed benches (F4), exact-coverage reconcile + deep provenance (F5), sparse variant column + validated ingestion (F3), playbook routing + M-sweep framing (F8), donor-dispatch proof. Nothing is certified; microbench scope, E2E PENDING.
